Pteridophyta (Greek; pteron-feather, phyta-plant), the name the given because of their feather like leaves. They are the cyptogams and first vascular plants. They are much advanced among non-flowering plant. The main plant body is sporophyte which produces spores. Mostly pteridophyta are herbaceous, but few of them are large tree which grow upto height of 30-40 feet. The study of pteridophyta is called pteridology. Theophrastus is called as father of pteridology.
2.6.2 CHARACTERISTICS FEATURES OF PTERIDOPHYTES Some of the basic features of pteridophytes are given below:

1. Pterodophytes grow in cool and shady terrestrial habitat. Few are aquatic. 2. Adult plant body is sporophyte and truly differentiated into leaves, stem and roots. 3. They are vascular plant having presence of both xylem and phloem tissue. 4. Leaves may simple, minute and sessile or petiolate. 5. The primary root is short lived which is replaced by adventitious roots. 6. The stems are usually herbaceous and branched monopodially or dichotomously.

7. Reproduction is through spores which are formed in sporangia. Sporangia develop on special structures, such as sori on the ventral surface of fertile leaves (fern), cones or strobili (Equisetum) or sporocarps (Marsilea, Azolla).
8. Plants are homosporous (all spores are of same size and structure) or heterosporous (spores of two different sizes).
9. The germination of spore give rise to multicellular, autotrophic (independent) gametophytic structure known as prothallus.
10. The sex organs, antheridia (male reproductive organs) and archegonia (female reproductive organs) develop on the prothallus.

11. The male gamete, antherozoid and female gamete, egg fuse to form a diploid oospore (Zygote). The fertilization takes place with the help of water. The oospore gives rise to sporophytic generation.
12. Alternation of generation is present in the life cycle.
Example: Dryopteris (fern), Lycopodium, Selaginella, Marsilea, etc.
Occurrence Dryopteris are found in moist and shady places. They are terrestrial plant, widely distributed all over the world.
Plant body The plant body is perennial, evergreen, vascular sporophytic and is differentiated into root, stem and leaves.
